title: Listening without prejudice
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When someone talks, are you listening or waiting to speak?
I said there are two things: paying attention is to something external, concentrating is to something internal. When the two come together, you are truly absorbing.

A student said the foundation is being open, hoping to understand their viewpoint. I said: how many of us listen but are not really open? We are closed, waiting for them to stop talking so that we can start talking.

Another student said: listening with the intent to understand, instead of listening with the intent to respond. It is kind of human nature to just think about what you are saying next. I remember the day a teacher told me, and I made a conscious process to change.

I said I listen without prejudice. I put my own frame down and look through the other person's perspective. If you do judge, you are vulnerable, and it has nothing to do with the other person. It has to do with your own mind.
I said it does not mean you will be best friends with that person. Let's not go to extremes.
A student said that people want to feel heard, and the listener who hears people out has a lot of influence and power just by being open-minded. I said: the silence becomes the power.

I asked: what about a person who does not communicate? How do you share differences of opinion without making people feel criticized? How do you make sure both sides are heard? How do you not undermine somebody else's message?
Which of those questions is the hardest for you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last time you waited to speak instead of listening.
Write who is hard for you to listen to.
Write what you would drop to look through their frame.
Write one question you will ask to understand, not to answer.
Write how you will tell they felt heard.

check.q: What did I say paying attention is directed at?
What did a student say to listen with the intent to do?
What did I say becomes the power?

recap: Listen to understand. Put your frame down. Silence is power.
